::: {.callout-note}
## Scope
Turn a set of `.qmd` into a Quarto **project**: a navigable, **branded website**, then make its
builds reproducible with **freeze** and render it to a publishable folder. Two challenges, one
project: each is its own hands-on part, with a break between them. Putting the site online is an
**optional last step** (Posit Connect Cloud, free account, no repository), so the folder is what
everyone leaves with. Everything runs on base-R `datasets::penguins` (R ≥ 4.5), so there's no data to download.

**Before you start:** work through the **[Setup page](../../setup.qmd)** if you haven't. Its
`00-check-setup.R` confirms R, Quarto, and the packages this lab uses. The optional branded-plot
stretch also uses `brand.yml`.
:::

**Starting point: a shipped set of pages.** You don't start from a blank folder. Open your
**`day2-projects/`** folder from the exercises download (double-click `day2-projects.Rproj`, see the
[Setup page](../../setup.qmd#get-the-materials)). It holds two content pages that already render on
their own but are **not yet a project**:

- `index.qmd` — a home page;
- `analysis.qmd` — a penguins analysis with a figure and a table.

Render one page to confirm it works: `quarto render analysis.qmd` gives a normal HTML page
(`analysis.html` right next to its source), since the folder isn't a project *yet*. Your job across the
two challenges is to make it a *site*, then ship it. Everything you render lands inside
`day2-projects/`. There's no project folder above it, so nothing redirects your output. A finished
reference is in **`solutions/day2/`** if you get stuck or fall behind.

## Website Challenge

> **Goal:** turn the `day2-projects/` pages into a navigable, **branded website** that renders locally to a
> `_site/` folder.

:::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks

::: {.column-margin}
{{< fa book-open >}} **Quarto docs**

[Websites](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) · [Brand](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/brand.html)
:::

1. In `day2-projects/`, create a **`_quarto.yml`** that declares the project and a website with navigation:
   ```yaml
   project:
     type: website
     output-dir: _site
   website:
     title: "Penguin Lab"
     navbar:
       left:
         - href: index.qmd
           text: Home
         - href: analysis.qmd
           text: Analysis
   format:
     html:
       theme: [cosmo, brand]
   ```
   The `theme:` list is a stack of layers, and **later layers win**. `brand` is the layer that
   reads your `_brand.yml` (you add that file in step 3), so it has to come *after* `cosmo` to
   override its colors. Until then `brand` adds nothing and you get plain `cosmo`.
2. **Render the whole folder**: from inside `day2-projects/`, run `quarto render` (or `quarto preview`).
   Because a `_quarto.yml` is now present, Quarto treats the folder as one project and builds **both**
   pages into `_site/`.
3. **Brand it.** Add a `day2-projects/_brand.yml` so the site shares one palette:
   ```yaml
   color:
     palette:
       teal: "#4C979F"
     primary: teal
   typography:
     fonts:
       - family: Albert Sans
         source: google
     base:
       family: Albert Sans
   ```
   Re-render. The navbar and links pick up the palette automatically, and the text is set in
   Albert Sans.
4. *(stretch)* Two things make the **within-page versus across-page** rule concrete. First, on
   `analysis.qmd`, drop `@tbl-means` into a sentence: it resolves to *Table 1* because the reference
   and its table share **one page** (exactly as yesterday). Second, notice `index.qmd` **already**
   links to the analysis with a plain Markdown link, `[analysis](analysis.qmd)`. That's deliberate,
   because **across** pages there is no auto-numbering (a *book* feature, not a website one), so a
   plain link is how you connect website pages.
::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see
A `day2-projects/_site/` folder with **two linked pages** and a **top navbar** (Home · Analysis); after the
brand step, the navbar and links turn **teal**, and the text is set in Albert Sans (headings keep
the body color). The plot keeps its default species colors: branding an R plot is a separate
`brand.yml`-package step, out of scope today. If you did the stretch,
the analysis page also shows a live **Table 1** reference (from `@tbl-means`) and the home page carries
a plain link into the analysis. Opening `_site/index.html` shows the home page; the navbar moves you to
the analysis page, whose figure is:
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint
- The `_quarto.yml` must sit **inside `day2-projects/`**: Quarto uses the *nearest* `_quarto.yml` as
  the project root, so this makes `day2-projects/` its own project. There's no `_quarto.yml` in any
  folder above it, so nothing else can claim your pages.
- `navbar:` items are `href` + `text`. `sidebar: { contents: auto }` builds a menu from the folder's
  files instead.
- `_brand.yml` is **auto-discovered** at the project root: no header line needed, just re-render.
- `quarto render` with no file argument builds the **whole project**; `quarto render index.qmd`
  builds one page.
:::

**The `solutions/day2/` folder is a reference, not a checklist.** The complete, known-good project lives
there in your exercises download: open it to compare your `_quarto.yml` / `_brand.yml`, or copy it
wholesale if you fell behind.

## Ship it Challenge

> **Goal:** make the project's builds **reproducible** with `freeze`, then render it to a publishable
> `_site/` folder. (Publishing to Pages is the watch-me demo. You produce the folder.)

::: {.callout-note}
## Starting point
Keep going with your Website Challenge `day2-projects/`. If you didn't finish it, open the ready-made
**`solutions/day2/`** project (a complete Part-1 site) and do the steps below in there.
:::

:::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks

::: {.column-margin}
{{< fa book-open >}} **Quarto docs**

[Freeze](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html#freeze) · [Publishing](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/)
:::

1. Add **freeze** to your project's `_quarto.yml` so unchanged pages aren't re-executed on every build:
   ```yaml
   execute:
     freeze: auto      # re-execute a document only when its own source changes
   ```
2. **See the skip.** Run `quarto render` once (the code runs; `_freeze/` is written). Run
   `quarto render` **again without editing**: the R cell is **skipped**, its result reused from
   `_freeze/` (the log shows no compute). For a *visible* tell, drop a cell with
   `cat(format(Sys.time()))` on `analysis.qmd`: on the frozen second render the printed timestamp does
   **not** change: a pass/fail you can see, not just an absence in the log. Now change the plot's
   **code** on `analysis.qmd` and re-render: only *that* page re-runs (and the timestamp finally ticks).
3. Find the shipped site under **`_site/`**: that folder *is* what you publish. Point any static host
   at it (an internal server, your department's pages, a hosting service).
4. *(optional, if there's time)* **Put it online.** From your project folder:
   ```bash
   quarto publish posit-connect-cloud
   ```
   The first run opens a browser to sign in (a free Posit account is enough, and no repository is
   needed), then uploads the `_site/` you just built. You get a URL you can open on your phone.
5. *(note, not a step)* `renv::snapshot()` writes an `renv.lock` that pins the packages: the second
   reproducibility leg, so a teammate (or CI) rebuilds the same environment.
::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see
On the **second** render (no edits between them), the log shows the R cell **skipped** (reused from
`_freeze/`), and the `cat(format(Sys.time()))` line prints the **same** time it did on the first render.
That frozen timestamp (and the quiet log) is exactly what lets CI render the site with no R at all.
Edit a page's code, and only that page re-runs, its timestamp finally advancing.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint
- `freeze: auto` re-executes a document when its **source** changes (prose or code) and reuses
  `_freeze/` when it hasn't, so an *unchanged* page never re-runs. `freeze: true` goes further: never
  re-execute on a project build (the CI mode).
- Frozen results live in `_freeze/`: commit that folder so CI can render without R.
- `output-dir` (default `_site`) is the whole deliverable: publish the folder, don't rebuild on the host.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution: the freeze block and the render flow

Add to your project's `_quarto.yml`:

``` yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

An optional visible tell: put this on `analysis.qmd`. A frozen render reuses the old value, so the
printed time stays put.

``` r
cat(format(Sys.time()))
```

From inside your project folder (`day2-projects/`):

``` bash
quarto render     # 1st build: runs the code, writes _freeze/ and _site/
quarto render     # 2nd build, no edits: the cell is skipped, timestamp unchanged
# then change the plot code on analysis.qmd and render again: only that page re-runs (time ticks)
```

To publish, point a host at `_site/`, or upload it with one command:

``` bash
quarto publish posit-connect-cloud
```
::::

## Troubleshooting

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=false}
## {{< fa wrench >}} If a render misbehaves
- **Rendered, but can't find the HTML?** Before you add `_quarto.yml`, a single-page render writes
  the HTML **next to its source** in `day2-projects/`. Once `_quarto.yml` is present, a project render
  collects both pages under `day2-projects/_site/`. Look in those two places.
- **YAML is indentation-sensitive.** If rendering fails *before* any code runs, check `_quarto.yml`
  for stray spaces, tabs, or unmatched quotes.
- **"No project" / pages don't link?** The `_quarto.yml` must be **inside `day2-projects/`**, and
  `href:` paths are relative to the source folder, **not** `_site/`.
- **Brand not applied?** Two causes. The file must be in `day2-projects/` (the project root), and
  `brand` must come **last** in the `theme:` list: `theme: [cosmo, brand]` gives you the palette,
  while `theme: cosmo` on its own keeps cosmo's colors and only the fonts change. Re-render after
  either fix. For
  **plots**, the palette needs `library(brand.yml)` + `theme_brand_ggplot2()` (the file alone doesn't
  reach ggplot).
- **A cross-reference shows `?@…`?** The cell label must start `fig-`/`tbl-`/`eq-` and be unique, and
  remember it only resolves **within one page** on a website.
- **Freeze didn't skip the cell?** It skips only when the source is **unchanged** since the last build:
  any edit (prose or code) re-runs that page. Delete `_freeze/` to force a clean rebuild.
- **Missing package?** `install.packages("<name>")` (or `renv::restore()`) and render again.
:::
